text:
Opened the Fintech Builders Summit this morning with Helena Voss-Marchetti, founder and CEO of Larchmont Systems. She's spent 20 years in payments infrastructure, built and sold a payments company, and sits on two bank boards. She knows where the weak points are.

Her core claim: small banks lose more to fraud per account than large banks, because they buy rules instead of models.

Larchmont's customers are banks under $5B in assets, and most have no data-science team. So they can't build their own models, and static rules are easy to probe.

Her answer is one shared model across 90 banks, trained on pooled, anonymised fraud labels. A small bank gets the benefit of fraud patterns it would never see on its own.

She also expects regulators to require explainable fraud decisions within two years. For anyone selling into banks, that's worth planning for now.

Best line of the morning: "A rule you can't update by Friday is a rule the fraudsters already know."

For those of us in GTM, the takeaway is that the buyers with the least technical capacity often have the most to gain, and the pitch has to work without a data team on their side.

What did you take from the keynote?
